full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim, J.: This Rule is directed against the order dated 30.6.93 passed by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate. Dhaka in Ramna PS case No. 126(8)92 under sections 326/307/302/34 of the Penal Code remanding the accused petitioner in the Police custody for 3 days. 

 2. The aforesaid case was started at the instance of one Md. Abdul Halim Khan, SI of Police on an FIR dated 31.8.92 with the Officer-in-Charge, Ramna PS on the allegations that there was an exchange of fire on 30.8.92 from 13.10 hours to 14-00 hours between two rival groups of students of Surja Sen Hall and Jasimuddin Hall; consequently one unknown person, aged about 30 years, was shot dead at the entrance gate of Surja Sen Hall, one Ali Hossain, a student of MA in history, Zahidur Rahman, a student of 2nd year Scierice of Zia Hall received bullet injuries on their persons and were under treatment in different hospitals. 

 3. The accused petitioner was arrested by the police on 3.9.92 and falsely implicated in Kotwali PS Case No. 31 (7) 92 under sections 394{302 Of the Penal Code and was further shown arrested in Sutrapur PS case No. 21(9)91 under sections 364/302/109/34 of the Penal Code on 7.9.91 and since then has been in jail custody. 

 4. Applications for bail in the aforesaid Kotwali and Sutrapur PS Cases were filed in the Court of the Sessions Judge, Dhaka in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 923 and 922 of 1993 respectively and the Additional Sessions Judge by order dated 21.6.93 was pleased to enlarge the accused petitioner on bail. 

 5. In order to frustrate the order of bail, the police in a malafide manner suppressing all relevant facts filed an application on 21.6.93 in the afternoon before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka for remand of the accused petitioner for seven days in Kotwali PS case No. 31(7)92 behind the back of the petitioner without even forwarding him before the Magistrate. The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate without assigning any reason allowed the remand of the accused petitioner in police custody for one day. 

 8. The Assistant Commissioner of Police (Detective) DAB, however, most illegally took the accused petitioner from Central Jail on remand in Kotwali PS Case to an unknown place and physically tortured him in an inhuman manner and again sent him to jail custody at 22.45 hours on 23.6.90 in seriously injured condition. Thereafter upon a prayer of the petitioner, the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate called for a report from DIG (Prison) and an explanation from the Investigating Officer. That the reports were received by the court on 26.6.93 and 25.6.93 respectively and on perusal of the same the court also called for a report regarding the physical condition of the accused petitioner from the Medical Officer, Dhaka, Central Jail and the same has not yet been received until the passing of the impugned order on 30.6.93. On 22.6.93 the Investigation Officer, in Ramna PS Case No. 126(8) 92 under sections 394/302 of the Penal Code filed. In application to the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka for showing the accused petitioner as being arrested in the case and also for remanding the accused in police custody for 5 days but the court allowed remand in police custody for 2 days. 

 9. On 24.6.93 an application on behalf of the accused petitioner was filed in the case for bail and also cancellation of the order of remand and upon hearing the parties, the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka rejected the prayer for bail but cancelled the order of remand with a direction to the Investigating Officer to submit a report regarding complicity of the accused in the case within a week. 

 On 26.6.93 the review application was taken up for consideration and upon hearing, the prayer was rejected On 29.6.93 the Investigating Officer of Ramna PS Case No. 126(8)92 filed an application with the recommendation of Assistant Police Commissioner, (Detective), DMP and public prosecutor for remand of the accused petitioner for 5 days alleging the petitioner is the leader of an armed terrorist group being in possession of arms as the group had committed terrorist activities in the city including Dhaka University Campus and created a reign of terror and during investigation it transpired that the accused was seen with other accused before the occurrence and for the sake of investigation and for recovery of arms it is necessary to interrogate him. 

 11. On 30.6.93 an application was filed on behalf of the accused petitioner for rejecting the prayer for remand and for directing the jail authority for arranging his proper treatment alleging torture by the police taking him to an unknown place in Kotwali PS Case No. 31(7)92 and asserting that previous order of remand having been cancelled no fresh order for remand can be passed. 

 13. Mr. Md Abu Bakkar Siddique, the learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the accused petitioner has submitted that the impugned order of remand of the accused petitioner, is in violation of the provision of section 16(1) and (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure as the accused was not forwarded to the court by the police and the same was passed in the absence of the accused and the same was also passed without perusal of the record, case diary and without ascertaining the actual condition under which the remand was asked for. The learned Advocate referred to the decision in the case of Khondakar Moshtaque Ahmed Vs. Bangladesh reported in 34 DLR (AD) 222. Mr. Siddique further submitted that the accused has been tortured in police custody in order to extract confessional statement from him and that the prayer for remand after about 10 months of his detention in jail custody is malafide and motivated. 

 14. Mr. AFM Shahid, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, has submitted that as the complicity of the accused transpired very recently in the case during the investigation and the accused was shown arrested in the case on 22.6.93 at a time when he was already in jail custody, is sufficient compliance of section 167 CrPC and the Magistrate lawfully allowed remand of the accused for the sake of investigation in the interest of justice. 

 "167(1)-Whenever any person is arrested and detained in custody, and it appears that the investigation cannot be completed within the period of twenty-four hours fixed by section 61; and there are grounds for believing that the accusation or information is well-founded, the Officer-in-Charge of the police-station (or the police-officer making the investigation if he is not below the rank of sub-Inspector) shall forthwith transmit to the nearest Magistrate a copy of the entries in the diary hereinafter prescribed relating to the case, and shall at the same time forward the accused to such Magistrate. " 

 Section 167(2)-The Magistrate to whom an accused person is forwarded under this section may, whether he has or has not jurisdiction to try the case, from time to time authorise the detention of the accused in such custody as such Magistrate thinks fit, for a term not exceeding fifteen days in the whole. If he has not jurisdiction to try the case or (send) it for trial, and considers further detention unnecessary, he may order the accused to be forwarded to a Magistrate having such jurisdiction: 

 "The requirement of the law is that the accused must be produced before a Magistrate after his arrest but the appellant was not produced before any Magistrate. Section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was holding the field and the Regulation 2(a) was promulgated on 28.12.76 that is, after a month. Section 167 CrPC required the production of the accused before Magistrate whether he has jurisdiction to try the case or not. This was to check any high handedness in the executive and as Khondaker Moshtaque Ahmed was not produced before any such Magistrate, the circumstances adds to the dimension of the contention that the arrest and subsequent proceeding was malafide". 

 15. The accused petitioner was arrested on 3.9.92 in connection with Kotwali PS Case No. 31 (7) 92 under sections 394/302 of the Penal Code upon an FIR dated 22.7.92 and he was subsequently shown arrested on 7.9.92 in Sutrapur PS Case No. 21(9)91 under sections 364/109/302/34 upon an FIR dated 10.9.91 for an occurrence dated 24.8.91 but in the instant case he was shown arrested on 22.6.93 in Ramna PS Case No. 126(8)92 under sections 326/307/302/34 of the Penal Code on an FIR dated 31.8.92 for an occurrence dated 30.8.92 i.e. after the lapse of about 9 (nine) months. 

 16. It appears from the application dated. 21.6.93 of the Police Inspector (DIB) that the prayer was made before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka for showing the accused arrested in Ramna PS Case No. 126 dated 31.8.92 and for 5 days remand without forwarding, the accused before the court and the court by order dated 22.6.92 (Annexure 'H') shown him arrested as prayed for and allowed 2 days' remand. On 24.6.93 an application on behalf of the accused petitioner was filed for cancellation of the order of remand as the same is designed to harass and torture the accused and the Court considering the facts and circumstances of the case cancelled the order of remand but rejected the prayer for bail. 

 19. It is not denied that at no point of time the accused was physically produced/ forwarded by the police to the Magistrate and without such forwarding the Court passed the order of remand to police custody for 3 days in Ramna PS Case No. 126(8)92. 

 20. The decision cited above is the authority for the proposition that the section 167 CrPC requires the production of the accused after his arrest by the police before a Magistrate whether he has jurisdiction to try the case or not and the same is to check any highhandedness in the act of the police. In the instant case the accused was already in judicial custody on 22.6.93 when the police prayed for showing him arrested in the instant case and allowing remand for the purpose of investigation and the Magistrate accordingly did the same. 

 21. Now the question in the aforesaid circumstances of the present case is whether there was any compliance of section 167 CrPC in view of the accused being already in judicial custody when the police simply prayed for showing the accused arrested in the instant case and for remand without actually forwarding the accused to Magistrate and the learned Court passed the order of remand without the accused being produced before the Court. Admittedly the police has not forwarded the accused to the Magistrate and the Magistrate also passed the order of remand in the absence of the accused being forwarded to him. 

 22. In the case of Mohd. Rafi Vs. State reported in (1969) Pakistan Criminal Law Journal 873 a single Judge of the Lahore High Court held that "The words of section 167 of the Criminal Procedure Code are clear that the accused is to be forwarded to a Magistrate and not that a Magistrate has to make himself available to the police in a building where a police lockup is situated. It is now established that when a Magistrate passes an order of remand to police custody under section 167 referred to above he performs a judicial function ............If the Magistrates are permitted to pass orders of remand in police stations where the accused admittedly have no means to have recourse to a lawyer or their relatives the whole significance of section 167 of the Criminal Procedure Code would disappear and it will amount to a farcical performance of imperative legal requirements concerning the liberty of the citizen". 

 23. It is also clear from the facts that the accused petitioner though shown arrested in the instant case but the offences for which he was arrested were not known to him or made known to him the non-production of an accused person before the Magistrate who does not know what is the charge against him and his subsequent order of remand in his absence without his production in the Court from the judicial custody where he is in a helpless and complete detachment from the outside world and where he has no freedom of communication with his lawyers or friends or relatives will actually amount to travesty of judicial procedure. 

 26. Admittedly the accused was arrested on 3.9.92 in connection with another case and has been in judicial custody since then but when the accused was shown arrested in the instant case on 22.6.93 he was not even intimated the offences for which he had been confined or permitting his friends/relatives to make access to him although he was shown arrested in the case on suspicion along with others in the course of police investigation about eight months after the alleged date of occurrence but a lawyer on his behalf allegedly took step in defending the accused without any instruction from the accused and instruction was not possible as he was not produced before the Magistrate. The whole purpose of production before the Magistrate was to make the accused aware of the offences levelled against him and the place where he was allowed remand, the purpose of the remand and his place and period of confinement, so that he can in case of necessity, communicate with his lawyer, relatives or friends and the Magistrate has a legal duty to check any high-handedness by the police. 

 28. In the instant case the accused has by his application, complained about the torture on him while in previous remand in connection with Kotwali PS Case No. 31 (7)91 and that he has been presently suffering, for which a medical report has already been called for and the allegation of torture has yet remained uncontroverted as no counter affidavit denying the allegation was filed in the Rule but the learned Magistrate did not ascertain the physical condition of the accused on production before him prior to the impugned order of remand and thus the learned Magistrate has failed to perform his judicial duties with vigilance in the protection of life and liberty of a citizen as guaranteed by law. 

 29. In the case of Jahangir Lal Vs. Emperor reported in 1935 AIR Lahore 230 it was held by a Division Bench of the Lahore High Court that "In all cases where remands are granted it is the duty of the Magistrate to inform the accused that he is a Magistrate, that a remand is applied for and to ask the accused how long he has been in police custody and whether he has any objection to offer to the remand". 

 31. In a recent Single Bench decision in the case of Naeemullah Vs. SSP Faisalabad and others 1992 Pakistan Criminal Law Journal 985 it was held that: 

 "The excesses of police by involving citizens in criminal cases without reasonable cause and through abuse of power vesting under section 54 CrPC are on increase. The learned Magistrate before whom the accuseds are produced for obtaining remand order are duty bound to consider each case on its own merits. They are not supposed to grant remand order mechanically. As the liberty of citizen is involved the Magistrates are required by law to act fairly and consciously. A citizen is not to be deprived of his liberty without due cause. It will therefore, be appropriate for a Magistrate not to pass the remand order as and when police appears before him. It would be appropriate for the Haq Magistrate to fix time when on each day the police must produce the accused for obtaining remand so that the members of the bar engaged by the accused are in a position to appear and represent the accused and oppose grant of remand." 

 35. We like to add that under section 439 CrPC this Court can suo motu call for the records and correct any error in the orders of the Court below, reference may be made to the decision in the case of Tofazzal Hossain Sheikh Vs. Mir Md. Akand and others 36 DLR (AD) 42 and accordingly we hold that the order dated 22.6.93 showing the accused arrested, and allowing remand was passed without complying with the provisions of section 167 CrPC and as such the order dated 22.6.93 and subsequent orders including the impugned order are illegal and not sustainable and as such liable to be set aside. 

 36. In the instant case the Magistrate may, however, pass necessary order against the accused on his production before him by the police and also. pass an order of remand afresh in accordance with law and in the light of the observation made hereinbefore, if prayer to that effect is made and if he considers the same in the interest of investigation.
